results.notes: When a clawback falls short, the reserved part (at most the shortfall) is recorded on the credit_debt flag. The flag gets details held, heldJobIds (the queued and processing jobs), outstanding, collected and reversal. releaseJob, for a job that such a flag names, takes the released credits back with a refund or chargeback movement keyed debt:<flag>:job:<job>, so once per job and flag. behaviorChanges: CCBILL_WEBHOOK_TOKEN is now required. Without it CCBill reports itself unconfigured (isConfigured and webhookConfigured are false, configurationProblem names the variable), checkout is unavailable and every CCBill webhook answers 503. Every CCBill webhook must carry ?token=. The .env.example and env.ts comments say so.

The CCBill NewSaleSuccess and NewSaleFailure event id is now '<eventType>:<subscriptionId>' (it was eventType:transactionId:timestamp). A signed sale re-posted with a new timestamp or transactionId is a duplicate.

For every processor, a purchase, pass start or renewal that is short of the item's price or in another currency is recorded as ignored (reason needs_review), raises a manual_review flag, and grants nothing. CCBill sales must bill exactly the item's price, and a pass needs recurring terms (R01).

A Segpay sale must carry an eticketid whose price point maps to exactly the claimed item, otherwise it is held for manual review. SEGPAY_PRICE_POINT_ID has no shared fallback, so an item without its own price point cannot be checked out (R02).

A refund, chargeback or cancellation that arrives before its purchase or pass start is kept as pending and applied, exactly once, when the purchase or pass lands (R10). Concurrent reversals of one payment are serialized (R18).

When a refund or chargeback cannot take back credits that creations in progress hold, those credits are recorded on the credit_debt flag (details: held, heldJobIds, outstanding, collected, reversal). They are taken back when those creations are cancelled or fail, and they no longer return to the person. The flag text no longer calls held credits 'spent' (R17).

A CCBill Cancellation or a Segpay Cancellation (stop rebilling) now sets the pass to the new status 'non_renewing'. The pass keeps its perks until current_period_end, and Expiration or Disable ends it. activePlan counts non_renewing. Payment history labels the event 'Renewal stopped' (R32).

Deleting an account sets its passes to canceled and raises a manual_review flag for each live pass on a real processor, asking an operator to cancel it at the processor. A renewal billed after deletion is held for review and grants no credits. The account.delete audit records passesEnded (R33).
A sale that lands for an account with an open chargeback flag, or for a deleted account, is held for manual review instead of granted, including sales from checkout links saved earlier (R38).

For Stripe, the pass credits from invoice.paid are recorded under the payment intent that paid the invoice, so a refund or dispute of a pass invoice claws back the credits and flags the account (R39).
/api/webhooks/payments/constructor, /toString and /__proto__ answer 404 instead of 500 (R40).

behaviorChanges: CCBill: pass-through values are read only as X-hlUser / X-hlItem / X-hlSig (any case). A NewSaleSuccess whose pair comes back without the X- prefix is recorded as 'ignored' and grants nothing (go-live question 1 in ccbill.ts updated).

They used to return 500 on every retry. Held pass-start events and their flags now carry subscriptionRef. A renewal for a subscription with no start at all still returns 500 so the processor retries.

CCBill: an unknown or missing billedCurrencyCode/currencyCode is recorded as currency 'xxx' (ISO 4217 'no currency') with the raw code in event metadata.currencyCode. Sales and renewals in it are held for manual review instead of being read as USD.
Stripe: a checkout session without amount_total or currency is recorded as 0 in 'xxx' and held for manual review (payment and subscription mode). It is no longer taken as the item's price.

Segpay: a Credit, Void or Charge with relatedtranid is matched only to that charge. If the charge hasn't landed, the reversal stays pending and is applied when it does, instead of being taken from the purchase's latest credited charge. Without relatedtranid the purchaseid fallback is unchanged. Sandbox reversals likewise match only their transactionRef. CCBill keeps the subscriptionId fallback until its reversal transactionId semantics are confirmed (ccbill.ts question 2).

All payment webhook processing now takes transaction-scoped Postgres advisory locks on the event's transaction and subscription/purchase refs before doing anything. Concurrent deliveries touching the same payment or pass are serialized (a delivery may wait for another in flight). A refund and its sale, or a cancellation and its pass start, can no longer both commit unseen.

behaviorChanges: Age verification is now required when either the account's stored jurisdiction or the current request's geo location requires it. A stored uncovered place no longer unlocks a GB or covered-US-state request. With no geo header on the request, the stored value decides alone.
POST /api/characters returns 451 age_verification_required to members in covered places who are not verified, the same as /api/uploads.

On a live deployment (isLiveDeployment), a 'verified' status from the sandbox provider reads as unverified, so those members are gated until they pass a real provider check.

Those outputs carry mediaWithheld: true and show 'Verify your age to see this'. GET /api/generations/:id/download and POST /api/templates (publish) return 451 for them.
Starting a new age check no longer overwrites with 'pending' a verification that completed while the new check was being opened.
/api/age-verification/return always redirects to /settings#age-verification, even when the provider's result API errors, times out or returns an unexpected shape. The check stays pending.

Anonymous visitors who have not passed the step-one 'I am 18 or older' gate (no hl_age_ok cookie) get no media URLs from GET /api/templates or from any page's discovery data. Signed-in members are unaffected.

behaviorChanges: Image uploads over 40 megapixels are refused with 413 too_large (checked from the header). Only the first frame of an animated or multi-page image is kept. Stored uploads are downscaled to fit 4096 px and flattened onto black (no alpha channel).

Video uploads are refused when longer than 60 s (422 too_long) or larger than 4096 px on a side (413 too_large); the scanner never clears such clips. Video is scanned across its whole length (once a second plus every sharp change), with frames downscaled to 1024 px.

With STORAGE_DRIVER=s3, the app never hands out presigned bucket URLs: all media, local or S3, is served through /api/media, which re-checks the asset on every request. S3 media traffic now passes through the web process. Browsers never contact S3_ENDPOINT, so the MinIO hosts-file step is gone.
/api/media streams only the requested byte range from storage; a file missing from storage is now 404 instead of 500.

Public (template) media is served only while a published, undeleted template uses it; otherwise only to its owner, read from the session cookie. Removing a template, unpublishing it or suspending its creator stops every link issued earlier at once.

Removing a reported template in the Reports panel soft-deletes its poster and preview, so they are purged after 30 days. For a report of a minor they are instead put on legal hold and get an open csam_report entry in the Abuse review queue.

The middleware no longer runs on POST /api/uploads and POST /api/characters, so bodies up to the documented 20 MB and 100 MB arrive whole. Those routes make the same Origin check themselves (403 bad_origin), refuse oversize bodies with 413 before reading them, and answer a body that is not a complete form with 400 invalid_form instead of 500.
Media links now live at most 1.1 x their TTL (private 300 to 330 s, public 3600 to 3960 s), down from almost 2 x. The Policies page says 'five minutes by default (at most half a minute more)'.
The download redirect (GET /api/generations/:id/download) points at APP_URL instead of the server's bind address.
A scan verdict that arrives after a match never overwrites it. The hourly purge re-checks legal hold per file under a row lock before deleting.

Docs updated: docs/engineering.md (upload limits, storage drivers, signed URLs, CSRF section), docs/deployment.md (STORAGE_DRIVER, S3_ENDPOINT, MinIO note), docs/abuse-response.md (video bounds, S3 serving, report removal), docs/drafts/information-architecture.md (no presigned URLs).

One ffmpeg pass writes the once-a-second PNGs and streams every frame at 128x128 yuv420p to pickChanges. The opening frame is always picked. Per-IP limits on sign-in, sign-up and signed-out takedowns key on the n-th X-Forwarded-For entry from the right (n = TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS; 0 means the right-most entry). The app must run behind a proxy with hops >= 1, because Next.js keeps a client-sent X-Forwarded-For when nothing is in front.
The sign-in email is trimmed and lowercased before the per-account limit and the lookup.

/auth?next= now redirects (when already signed in) and lands after the form only on a same-origin path (pathname+search+hash). Anything that would resolve to another origin, or normalizes to //host, goes to /.
Deleting an account now sets its handle to deleted_<full user id> instead of deleted_<first 8 chars>.
PATCH /api/me: two people claiming the same handle at once now gets the loser a 409 handle_taken instead of a 500.

Logs and the error webhook: for Postgres data errors (SQLSTATE class 22), the value quoted in the message, such as a date of birth, is replaced with [redacted]. The query statement and the failure kind are kept.

Rate limits and /api/health use a separate Redis client that gives up after one reconnect or 2 s. During a Redis outage every rate-limited route (login, signup, takedowns, uploads, drafts, checkout, characters, reports, push subscribe, age-verification start) answers 503 {code: "unavailable"} and logs "rate limiter unavailable". Sign-up rejects dates of birth that are not real calendar days (e.g. 2000-02-30, 1990-13-01) with 422 and the field error "Enter a real date of birth." instead of a 500.

attempts.attempt: Another way to the same behavior: the account-deletion password re-check, DELETE /api/me { password }, which runs bcrypt cost 12.
attempts.test: tests/integration/attack-auth.test.ts "R05 attack: other ways to the same behaviour > the password re-check on account deletion is attempt-limited like sign-in" (it.fails)
attempts.details: HOLE, medium. deleteAccount (src/server/auth/account.ts:163-165) calls verifyPassword, and src/app/api/me/route.ts:22-29 has no rateLimit. Unmarked run: "expected 12 to be less than or equal to 10": all 12 wrong guesses got 403, none got 429, about 0.5 s of bcrypt each. Two consequences. A stolen session can guess the password without limit; a correct guess deletes the account but reveals a password that may be reused elsewhere. More importantly, any member can drive unlimited bcrypt-12 work from one account: the CPU-exhaustion vector R05 names for sign-in (its suggested fix is a global limit on bcrypt work), now reachable with one account, and sign-up gives 10 accounts per hour per IP (unlimited per IPv6 /64 via H1).

attempts.attempt: Regression in nearby behavior (the limiter R05 relies on, changed by R30): make the connection fail between rateLimit()'s INCR and its EXPIRE.
attempts.test: tests/integration/attack-auth.test.ts "R05 attack: other ways to the same behaviour > a failure between INCR and EXPIRE does not leave a bucket that never expires" (it.fails)
attempts.details: HOLE, low. src/server/redis.ts rateLimit() sends INCR and then, only when count === 1, a separate EXPIRE. The test makes requestRedis().expire reject once ('Connection is closed.'). The request correctly fails closed with 503, but the unmarked run shows "expected -1 to be greater than 0": the counter keeps no TTL. Because EXPIRE only runs at count 1, that bucket never expires: once it passes the limit (a member's login:email bucket, an address's signup bucket) it answers 429 until someone deletes the key. This was possible before on a process crash between the two commands. R30's fail-fast client (maxRetriesPerRequest 1, commandTimeout 2000) makes it reachable on a short Redis disconnect. Fix direction: a MULTI or Lua INCR+EXPIRE, or SET NX EX followed by INCR.

behaviorChanges: When util.inspect or console.error formats a DrizzleQueryError, in the web server or the worker, the error now redacts itself in place first. Prints show 'params: [redacted]' with the query text and frames kept. This applies to the error itself and to it as a cause at any depth, so dev-time prints of query errors no longer show bound values either.

Next.js's own ' ⨯' print for App Router page render errors and its console.error for route handlers that throw past route() no longer contain query parameters, even though Next prints before instrumentation's onRequestError runs.

scrubQueryParams (used by onRequestError) walks the whole cause chain, not only five errors deep. It also replaces the driver's `detail` field (Postgres's 'Failing row contains (...)' / 'Key (...)=(...) already exists.') with '[redacted]' on every error in the chain, so printed causes show detail: '[redacted]'.

Structured log lines: any string field (not only Error values) that contains a Drizzle '\nparams: ...' section now has it replaced by 'params: [redacted]', at every level (e.g. push.notify_failed err, generation.provider_error message, generation.store_failed err).

src/instrumentation.ts doc comment corrected: Next prints App Router page and route handler errors before the hook and other errors after it. Query errors scrub themselves when printed (scrubWhenInspected, installed by src/server/db), and the hook still scrubs the reported error in place.
